source.text: וַיַּגִּ֥דוּ לְדָוִ֖ד לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֤ה פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ נִלְחָמִ֣ים בִּקְעִילָ֔ה וְהֵ֖מָּה שֹׁסִ֥ים אֶת־הַגֳּרָנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And told to David, saying, Look, Philistines [are] fighting against Keilah, and they [are] plundering the threshing floors.

en.L: And they told David, saying, "Look, [the] Philistines [are] fighting against Keilah, and they [are] plundering the threshing floors."
en.B: David was told, "The Philistines are attacking Keilah and looting the threshing floors."
en.R: Someone brought David this news: "The Philistines are attacking the town of Keilah. They are stealing the grain from the threshing floors."

es.L: Y le avisaron a David, diciendo: «He aquí que [los] filisteos [están] peleando contra Keila, y [están] saqueando las eras».
es.B: A David le avisaron: «Los filisteos están atacando Keila y saqueando las eras».
es.R: Alguien le trajo a David esta noticia: «Los filisteos están atacando el pueblo de Keila. Están robando el grano de las eras».

fr.L: Et on le rapporta à David, en disant : « Voici, les Philistins combattent contre Qeïla, et ils pillent les aires. »
fr.B: On vint dire à David : « Les Philistins attaquent Qeïla et pillent les aires de battage. »
fr.R: Quelqu’un est venu annoncer à David : « Les Philistins attaquent la ville de Qeïla. Ils volent le grain sur les aires de battage. »

sw.L: Wakamwambia Daudi, wakisema, "Tazama, Wafilisti wanapigana na Keila, nao wanateka nyara viwanja vya kupuria nafaka."
sw.B: Daudi akaambiwa, "Wafilisti wanaushambulia Keila na kuteka nyara viwanja vya kupuria nafaka."
sw.R: Mtu mmoja akamletea Daudi habari hii: "Wafilisti wanaushambulia mji wa Keila. Wanaiba nafaka kutoka kwenye viwanja vya kupuria."

vi.L: Người ta báo cho Đa-vít rằng: "Kìa, người Phi-li-tin đang đánh Kê-i-la, và họ đang cướp các sân đạp lúa."
vi.B: Có người báo cho Đa-vít: "Người Phi-li-tin đang tấn công Kê-i-la và cướp phá các sân đạp lúa."
vi.R: Có người đem tin đến cho Đa-vít: "Người Phi-li-tin đang tấn công thành Kê-i-la. Họ đang cướp lúa ở các sân đạp lúa."

ko.L: 그리고 사람들이 다윗에게 알려 말했다. "보십시오, 블레셋 사람들이 그일라를 치고 타작마당들을 약탈하고 있습니다."
ko.B: 누군가가 다윗에게 알렸다. "블레셋 사람들이 그일라를 공격하여 타작마당을 약탈하고 있습니다."
ko.R: 어떤 사람이 다윗에게 이런 소식을 전했다. "블레셋 사람들이 그일라 성을 공격하고 있습니다. 타작마당에 있는 곡식을 빼앗아 가고 있습니다."

pt.L: E contaram a Davi, dizendo: "Eis que os filisteus [estão] lutando contra Queila, e eles [estão] saqueando as eiras."
pt.B: Disseram a Davi: "Os filisteus estão atacando Queila e saqueando as eiras."
pt.R: Alguém trouxe esta notícia a Davi: "Os filisteus estão atacando a cidade de Queila. Eles estão roubando os cereais das eiras."

decisions.choice: Keilah: a walled town in the lowland of Judah, near the Philistine border
decisions.reason: Keilah is listed among the towns of the western foothills of Judah (Joshua 15:33, 44). It lay a few hours' walk from Philistine territory, and it had gates and bars (verse 7).

decisions.choice: the threshing floors: where the harvested grain lay
decisions.reason: At harvest the grain was brought to open, hard-packed floors to be threshed and winnowed. Raiders who took it there carried off the town's food for the year, as Midian had done to Israel (Judges 6:3-4, 11).

decisions.choice: they told David: someone brought word; the speakers are not named
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject and works like a passive: "David was told". David was then in the forest of Hereth in Judah (22:5).

decisions.choice: stealing the grain from the threshing floors
decisions.reason: Readable says what was taken from the threshing floors, and adds "the town of" before the name.

decisions.choice: Qeïla
decisions.reason: A name not in the terms table, in the usual French transcription of the Hebrew, kept the same through both books.

decisions.choice: Keila
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish form of the town's name (m1), kept through the chapter.

decisions.choice: "Keila"
decisions.reason: Place names not in the terms note take a Swahili spelling and are kept through the block.

decisions.choice: "그일라" for Keilah
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant Korean form of the name, kept the same through both books.

decisions.choice: Queila; as eiras
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also verses 2-13): "Queila", the form of Joshua 15:44 in Portuguese. "Eira" is the ordinary Portuguese word for the hard-packed floor where grain was threshed (m2); Readable says what was taken from it, as the English does.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֨ל דָּוִ֤ד בַּֽיהוָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַאֵלֵ֣ךְ וְהִכֵּ֔יתִי בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּהסוַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־דָּוִ֗ד לֵ֚ךְ וְהִכִּ֣יתָ בַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְהוֹשַׁעְתָּ֖ אֶת־קְעִילָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And inquired David of Yahweh, saying, Shall I go and strike these the Philistines? And said Yahweh to David, Go, and strike the Philistines and save Keilah.

en.L: And David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "Shall I go and strike these Philistines?" And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to David, "Go, and strike the Philistines and save Keilah."
en.B: So David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Am I to go and attack these Philistines?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered David, "Go, attack the Philistines, and rescue Keilah."
en.R: David asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Should I go and fight these Philistines?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told him, "Go. Fight the Philistines and save Keilah."

es.L: Y consultó David {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, diciendo: «¿Iré y heriré a estos filisteos?». Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a David: «Ve, y hiere a los filisteos y salva a Keila».
es.B: Así que David consultó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «¿Debo ir a atacar a estos filisteos?». {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le respondió a David: «Ve, ataca a los filisteos y libra a Keila».
es.R: David le preguntó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «¿Debo ir a pelear contra estos filisteos?». {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo: «Ve. Pelea contra los filisteos y salva a Keila».

fr.L: Et David consulta {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, en disant : « Irai-je, et frapperai-je ces Philistins ? » Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à David : « Va, et frappe les Philistins, et sauve Qeïla. »
fr.B: David consulta donc {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : « Dois-je aller attaquer ces Philistins ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} répondit à David : « Va, attaque les Philistins et délivre Qeïla. »
fr.R: David a demandé {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « Est-ce que je dois aller combattre ces Philistins ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a répondu : « Va. Combats les Philistins et sauve Qeïla. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akisema, "Je, niende nikawapige Wafilisti hawa?" {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Daudi, "Nenda, ukawapige Wafilisti na kuuokoa Keila."
sw.B: Basi Daudi akamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Je, niende kuwashambulia Wafilisti hawa?" {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamjibu Daudi, "Nenda, uwashambulie Wafilisti na kuuokoa Keila."
sw.R: Daudi akamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Je, niende kupigana na Wafilisti hawa?" {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia, "Nenda. Pigana na Wafilisti, uuokoe Keila."

vi.L: Đa-vít cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} rằng: "Con có nên đi đánh những người Phi-li-tin này không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Đa-vít: "Hãy đi, đánh người Phi-li-tin và giải cứu Kê-i-la."
vi.B: Vậy Đa-vít cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Con có nên đi tấn công những người Phi-li-tin này không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp với Đa-vít: "Hãy đi tấn công người Phi-li-tin và giải cứu Kê-i-la."
vi.R: Đa-vít hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Con có nên đi đánh những người Phi-li-tin này không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với ông: "Hãy đi. Hãy đánh người Phi-li-tin và cứu Kê-i-la."

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈어 말했다. "제가 가서 이 블레셋 사람들을 칠까요?" 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 다윗에게 말씀하셨다. "가서 블레셋 사람들을 치고 그일라를 구원하여라."
ko.B: 다윗이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈었다. "제가 가서 이 블레셋 사람들을 쳐야 합니까?" {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 다윗에게 대답하셨다. "가서 블레셋 사람들을 치고 그일라를 구하여라."
ko.R: 다윗이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈었다. "제가 가서 이 블레셋 사람들과 싸워야 합니까?" {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 다윗에게 말씀하셨다. "가거라. 블레셋 사람들과 싸워서 그일라를 구하여라."

pt.L: E Davi consultou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, dizendo: "Irei e ferirei estes filisteus?" E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Davi: "Vai, e fere os filisteus, e salva Queila."
pt.B: Então Davi consultou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: "Devo ir e atacar estes filisteus?" {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} respondeu a Davi: "Vai, ataca os filisteus e livra Queila."
pt.R: Davi perguntou {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}: "Devo ir lutar contra esses filisteus?" {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} respondeu: "Vai. Luta contra os filisteus e salva Queila."

decisions.choice: inquired of the LORD: asked God for an answer, probably through a priest or prophet
decisions.reason: Israel sought the LORD's will through the priest with the ephod, or through a prophet (10:22; 14:36-37; 28:6). The prophet Gad was with David (22:5), and verse 6 explains that Abiathar the priest came to him with an ephod. The text does not say which way David asked here.

decisions.choice: save Keilah: rescue it, the work of Israel's deliverers
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the LORD saving Israel through the judges and through Saul himself (Judges 2:16; 1 Samuel 9:16; 11:3). Saul is the king, yet it is David, hunted by Saul, who is sent to rescue a town of Judah.

decisions.choice: asked
decisions.reason: Readable says "asked" for "inquired of", as at 10:22.

decisions.choice: "kumwuliza BWANA"
decisions.reason: As the terms note: inquiring of the LORD is "kumwuliza BWANA" at every level, through this block.

decisions.choice: David asks God in the formal polite style (합쇼체; Literal "칠까요" keeps a plainer question); God answers in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: People speak to God in 합쇼체 and God speaks 해라체, as the terms of this translation set.

decisions.choice: David asks God as "con"; God answers with a plain command
decisions.reason: People speak to God in prayer forms (Genesis terms note); God speaks to David without a pronoun here, and where one is needed calls him "ngươi" at Literal and "con" at Balanced and Readable (2:27).

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמְר֜וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י דָוִד֙ אֵלָ֔יו הִנֵּ֨ה אֲנַ֥חְנוּ פֹ֛ה בִּֽיהוּדָ֖ה יְרֵאִ֑ים וְאַף֙ כִּֽי־נֵלֵ֣ךְ קְעִלָ֔ה אֶל־מַֽעַרְכ֖וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] men of David to him, Look, we here in Judah [are] afraid, and how much more if we go [to] Keilah against [the] battle lines of [the] Philistines.

en.L: And David's men said to him, "Look, we [are] afraid here in Judah; how much more if we go [to] Keilah against the battle lines of [the] Philistines!"
en.B: But David's men said to him, "Even here in Judah we live in fear. How much worse if we go to Keilah to face the Philistine army!"
en.R: But David's men said to him, "We are afraid even here in Judah. It will be much worse if we go to Keilah and fight the Philistine army!"

es.L: Y le dijeron los hombres de David: «He aquí que nosotros aquí en Judá tenemos miedo; ¡cuánto más si vamos a Keila contra las filas de los filisteos!».
es.B: Pero los hombres de David le dijeron: «Aun aquí en Judá vivimos con miedo. ¡Cuánto peor si vamos a Keila a enfrentarnos con el ejército filisteo!».
es.R: Pero los hombres de David le dijeron: «Tenemos miedo aun aquí en Judá. ¡Será mucho peor si vamos a Keila a pelear contra el ejército filisteo!».

fr.L: Et les hommes de David lui dirent : « Voici, nous avons peur ici en Juda ; combien plus si nous allons à Qeïla contre les rangs des Philistins ! »
fr.B: Mais les hommes de David lui dirent : « Ici même, en Juda, nous vivons dans la peur. Que sera-ce si nous allons à Qeïla affronter l’armée des Philistins ! »
fr.R: Mais les hommes de David lui ont dit : « Nous avons peur même ici, en Juda. Ce sera bien pire si nous allons à Qeïla pour combattre l’armée des Philistins ! »

sw.L: Watu wa Daudi wakamwambia, "Tazama, sisi tunaogopa hapa katika Yuda; sembuse tukienda Keila kupambana na safu za vita za Wafilisti!"
sw.B: Lakini watu wa Daudi wakamwambia, "Hata hapa katika Yuda tunaishi kwa hofu. Itakuwa vibaya zaidi kama nini tukienda Keila kukabiliana na jeshi la Wafilisti!"
sw.R: Lakini watu wa Daudi wakamwambia, "Tunaogopa hata hapa Yuda. Itakuwa vibaya zaidi sana tukienda Keila kupigana na jeshi la Wafilisti!"

vi.L: Những người của Đa-vít nói với ông: "Kìa, ở đây trong Giu-đa chúng tôi [còn] sợ, huống chi nếu chúng tôi đi [đến] Kê-i-la đánh các hàng quân Phi-li-tin!"
vi.B: Nhưng những người theo Đa-vít nói với ông: "Ngay ở đây trong Giu-đa chúng tôi đã sống trong sợ hãi. Huống chi đi đến Kê-i-la đối đầu với quân Phi-li-tin!"
vi.R: Nhưng những người theo Đa-vít nói với ông: "Ngay ở đây trong Giu-đa chúng tôi cũng sợ. Nếu đi đến Kê-i-la đánh quân Phi-li-tin thì còn tệ hơn nhiều!"

ko.L: 그러자 다윗의 부하들이 그에게 말했다. "보십시오, 우리는 여기 유다에서도 두려워하고 있는데, 하물며 그일라로 가서 블레셋 사람들의 전열과 맞서면 어떻겠습니까!"
ko.B: 그러나 다윗의 부하들이 그에게 말했다. "우리는 여기 유다에 있으면서도 두려워하며 지냅니다. 하물며 그일라로 가서 블레셋 군대와 맞서면 얼마나 더하겠습니까!"
ko.R: 그러나 다윗의 부하들이 다윗에게 말했다. "우리는 여기 유다에서도 무서워하고 있습니다. 그일라로 가서 블레셋 군대와 싸우면 훨씬 더 위험할 것입니다!"

pt.L: E os homens de Davi lhe disseram: "Eis que nós aqui em Judá [estamos] com medo; quanto mais se formos [a] Queila contra as fileiras dos filisteus!"
pt.B: Mas os homens de Davi lhe disseram: "Mesmo aqui em Judá vivemos com medo. Quanto pior será se formos a Queila enfrentar o exército dos filisteus!"
pt.R: Mas os homens de Davi disseram a ele: "Nós estamos com medo até aqui em Judá. Vai ser muito pior se formos a Queila lutar contra o exército dos filisteus!"

decisions.choice: how much more: an argument from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: The two words make the second case stronger than the first: if they are afraid where they are, they will be far more afraid facing an army in battle.

decisions.choice: here in Judah: where they were hiding from Saul
decisions.reason: Keilah also belonged to Judah, so the contrast is not between two territories. In the hills of Judah the men were already in danger from Saul; at Keilah they would have the Philistines in front of them as well.

decisions.choice: battle lines: an army drawn up for battle
decisions.reason: The word means ranks set in order for fighting, as when the Philistines and Israel faced each other in the Valley of Elah (17:8, 10).

decisions.choice: the Philistine army
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the army that stands in battle lines rather than the lines themselves.

decisions.choice: David's men say "ông" to David and "chúng tôi" for themselves; David calls them "anh em"
decisions.reason: The leader of a band of outlaws and his men; respectful but not courtly. This holds through the block.

decisions.choice: David's men speak to him in the formal polite style (합쇼체); David speaks to them in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: The leader of a band and his men, as the king and his officials; the same forms hold for David and his men through the rest of the book.

source.text: וַיּ֨וֹסֶף ע֤וֹד דָּוִד֙ לִשְׁאֹ֣ל בַּֽיהוָ֔הסוַֽיַּעֲנֵ֖הוּ יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר ק֚וּם רֵ֣ד קְעִילָ֔ה כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י נֹתֵ֛ן אֶת־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים בְּיָדֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And added again David to inquire of Yahweh, and answered him Yahweh and said, Arise, go down [to] Keilah, for I [am] giving Philistines into your hand.

en.L: And David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} yet again, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered him and said, "Arise, go down [to] Keilah, for I am giving [the] Philistines into your hand."
en.B: David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} once more, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered him, "Set out and go down to Keilah, for I am handing the Philistines over to you."
en.R: So David asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} again, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} answered him, "Go down to Keilah now. I am going to give you victory over the Philistines."

es.L: Y volvió David a consultar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le respondió y dijo: «Levántate, baja a Keila, porque yo entrego a los filisteos en tu mano».
es.B: David consultó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} una vez más, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le respondió: «Ponte en marcha y baja a Keila, porque voy a entregarte a los filisteos».
es.R: Así que David le preguntó otra vez {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le respondió: «Baja ahora a Keila. Te voy a dar la victoria sobre los filisteos».

fr.L: Et David consulta encore une fois {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui répondit et dit : « Lève-toi, descends à Qeïla, car je livre les Philistins dans ta main. »
fr.B: David consulta {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} une fois de plus, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui répondit : « Mets-toi en route et descends à Qeïla, car je te livre les Philistins. »
fr.R: Alors David a encore posé la question {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a répondu : « Descends à Qeïla maintenant. Je vais te donner la victoire sur les Philistins. »

sw.L: Daudi akamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} tena, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamjibu, akasema, "Inuka, ushuke Keila, kwa maana ninawatia Wafilisti mkononi mwako."
sw.B: Daudi akamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mara nyingine, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamjibu, "Ondoka, ushuke Keila, kwa maana ninawatia Wafilisti mikononi mwako."
sw.R: Basi Daudi akamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} tena, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamjibu, "Shuka Keila sasa. Nitakupa ushindi juu ya Wafilisti."

vi.L: Đa-vít lại cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} lần nữa, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trả lời ông: "Hãy đứng dậy đi xuống Kê-i-la, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phó người Phi-li-tin vào tay ngươi."
vi.B: Đa-vít cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} một lần nữa, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp: "Hãy lên đường đi xuống Kê-i-la, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phó người Phi-li-tin vào tay con."
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} lần nữa, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp: "Hãy đi xuống Kê-i-la ngay. {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ cho con thắng người Phi-li-tin."

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 다시 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈었다. 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 대답하여 말씀하셨다. "일어나 그일라로 내려가거라. 내가 블레셋 사람들을 네 손에 넘겨주겠다."
ko.B: 다윗은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 한 번 더 여쭈었다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 대답하셨다. "일어나 그일라로 내려가거라. 내가 블레셋 사람들을 네 손에 넘겨주겠다."
ko.R: 그래서 다윗은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 다시 여쭈었다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 대답하셨다. "지금 그일라로 내려가거라. 내가 너에게 블레셋 사람들을 이기게 해 주겠다."

pt.L: E Davi tornou a consultar {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} lhe respondeu e disse: "Levanta-te, desce [a] Queila, pois eu estou entregando os filisteus na tua mão."
pt.B: Davi consultou {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} mais uma vez, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} lhe respondeu: "Parte e desce a Queila, pois eu vou entregar os filisteus nas tuas mãos."
pt.R: Então Davi perguntou de novo {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}}, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} lhe respondeu: "Desce agora a Queila. Eu vou te dar a vitória sobre os filisteus."

decisions.choice: inquired again: a second asking, because of the men's fear
decisions.reason: David asks the same question a second time after his men object (verse 3). The second answer repeats the first and adds a promise of victory, which answers their fear.

decisions.choice: giving into your hand: giving you power over them, victory
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power. The participle "giving" presents the victory as already under way.

decisions.choice: go down: from the hill country to the lower foothills
decisions.reason: Keilah lies in the foothills west of the hills of Judah, so David's men must go down to reach it, as Saul's men would (verse 8).

decisions.choice: Set out (Balanced); now (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Arise" here means to get moving, not to stand up. Balanced says "set out"; Readable gives the sense of urgency with "now".

decisions.choice: give you victory over
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom "give into your hand".

source.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִד֩ וַאֲנָשָׁ֨יו קְעִילָ֜ה וַיִּלָּ֣חֶם בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֗ים וַיִּנְהַג֙ אֶת־מִקְנֵיהֶ֔ם וַיַּ֥ךְ בָּהֶ֖ם מַכָּ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣שַׁע דָּוִ֔ד אֵ֖ת יֹשְׁבֵ֥י קְעִילָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And went David and his men [to] Keilah, and fought against the Philistines, and drove off their livestock, and struck them [with] a great striking; and saved David [the] inhabitants of Keilah.

en.L: So David and his men went [to] Keilah and fought against the Philistines, and he drove off their livestock and struck them [with] a great blow. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.
en.B: So David and his men went to Keilah and fought the Philistines. He carried off their livestock and dealt them a heavy defeat. So David rescued the people of Keilah.
en.R: So David and his men went to Keilah and fought the Philistines. David took away their animals and killed a great many of them. That is how David saved the people of Keilah.

es.L: Y fueron David y sus hombres a Keila, y pelearon contra los filisteos, y se llevó su ganado, y los hirió con gran estrago. Así salvó David a los habitantes de Keila.
es.B: David y sus hombres fueron a Keila y pelearon contra los filisteos. Se llevó su ganado y les infligió una gran derrota. Así libró David a la gente de Keila.
es.R: Entonces David y sus hombres fueron a Keila y pelearon contra los filisteos. David se llevó los animales de ellos y mató a muchísimos. Así fue como David salvó a la gente de Keila.

fr.L: Et David et ses hommes allèrent à Qeïla, et ils combattirent contre les Philistins, et il emmena leur bétail, et il les frappa d’un grand coup. Et David sauva les habitants de Qeïla.
fr.B: David et ses hommes allèrent donc à Qeïla et combattirent les Philistins. Il emmena leur bétail et leur infligea une lourde défaite. Ainsi David délivra les habitants de Qeïla.
fr.R: Alors David et ses hommes sont allés à Qeïla et ils ont combattu les Philistins. David a emmené leurs bêtes et il a tué un très grand nombre de Philistins. C’est ainsi que David a sauvé les habitants de Qeïla.

sw.L: Daudi na watu wake wakaenda Keila, wakapigana na Wafilisti, akawachukua mifugo yao, akawapiga pigo kuu. Hivyo Daudi akawaokoa wakaaji wa Keila.
sw.B: Basi Daudi na watu wake wakaenda Keila, wakapigana na Wafilisti. Akachukua mifugo yao, akawashinda vibaya sana. Hivyo Daudi akawaokoa watu wa Keila.
sw.R: Basi Daudi na watu wake wakaenda Keila, wakapigana na Wafilisti. Daudi akachukua wanyama wao, akawaua wengi sana. Hivyo ndivyo Daudi alivyowaokoa watu wa Keila.

vi.L: Vậy Đa-vít và những người của ông đi [đến] Kê-i-la, đánh người Phi-li-tin, lùa gia súc của họ đi và đánh họ một trận lớn. Như vậy Đa-vít giải cứu dân cư Kê-i-la.
vi.B: Vậy Đa-vít và thuộc hạ đi đến Kê-i-la đánh người Phi-li-tin. Ông lùa gia súc của họ đi và gây cho họ một thất bại nặng nề. Như thế Đa-vít đã giải cứu dân thành Kê-i-la.
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít và thuộc hạ đi đến Kê-i-la đánh người Phi-li-tin. Đa-vít bắt gia súc của họ và giết rất nhiều người trong số họ. Đó là cách Đa-vít cứu dân thành Kê-i-la.

ko.L: 그래서 다윗과 그의 부하들이 그일라로 가서 블레셋 사람들과 싸웠고, 그는 그들의 가축을 몰아 오고 그들을 크게 쳐부수었다. 이렇게 다윗이 그일라 주민들을 구원했다.
ko.B: 다윗과 그의 부하들은 그일라로 가서 블레셋 사람들과 싸웠다. 다윗은 그들의 가축을 끌어오고 그들을 크게 무찔렀다. 이렇게 다윗은 그일라 사람들을 구해 냈다.
ko.R: 그래서 다윗과 그의 부하들은 그일라로 가서 블레셋 사람들과 싸웠다. 다윗은 그들의 가축을 빼앗고, 그들을 아주 많이 죽였다. 이렇게 해서 다윗은 그일라 사람들을 구했다.

pt.L: Assim Davi e os seus homens foram [a] Queila e lutaram contra os filisteus, e ele levou o gado deles e os feriu [com] um grande golpe. Assim Davi salvou os moradores de Queila.
pt.B: Então Davi e os seus homens foram a Queila e lutaram contra os filisteus. Ele levou os animais deles e lhes impôs uma grande derrota. Assim Davi livrou os moradores de Queila.
pt.R: Então Davi e os seus homens foram a Queila e lutaram contra os filisteus. Davi tomou os animais deles e matou um grande número de filisteus. Foi assim que Davi salvou o povo de Queila.

decisions.choice: his men: the written text uses an older spelling of the same word
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell "his men" in a short, older form; the scribes' marginal reading gives the usual form. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: drove off their livestock: took the Philistines' animals as plunder
decisions.reason: The text does not say why the Philistines had livestock with them; they may have brought animals for food or to carry off the stolen grain. Taking them turned the raiders' own goods into spoil.

decisions.choice: David saved Keilah: what the LORD promised is done
decisions.reason: The verse ends with the word the LORD used in verse 2, "save Keilah". The story shows the promise kept to the letter.

decisions.choice: killed a great many of them
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what a "great blow" meant in battle.

decisions.choice: salvou (L, R); livrou (B)
decisions.reason: Each level uses the same verb here as in the LORD's command of verse 2 ("salva Queila", "livra Queila"), so that the promise is seen to be kept word for word (m3).

source.text: וַיְהִ֗י בִּ֠בְרֹחַ אֶבְיָתָ֧ר בֶּן־אֲחִימֶ֛לֶךְ אֶל־דָּוִ֖ד קְעִילָ֑ה אֵפ֖וֹד יָרַ֥ד בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, in fleeing Abiathar son of Ahimelech to David [to] Keilah, an ephod came down in his hand.

en.L: And it was, when Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled to David [at] Keilah, an ephod came down in his hand.
en.B: Now when Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, he came down with an ephod in his hand.
en.R: When Abiathar son of Ahimelech escaped and came to David at Keilah, he brought an ephod with him. The ephod was the priest's vest used to ask God for answers.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando Abiatar hijo de Ahimelec huyó a David [en] Keila, bajó con un efod en su mano.
es.B: Cuando Abiatar hijo de Ahimelec huyó a reunirse con David en Keila, bajó con un efod en la mano.
es.R: Cuando Abiatar hijo de Ahimelec escapó y llegó a donde estaba David en Keila, trajo consigo un efod. El efod era el chaleco del sacerdote que se usaba para pedirle respuestas a Dios.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand Abiathar, fils d’Ahimélek, s’enfuit auprès de David à Qeïla, qu’un éphod descendit dans sa main.
fr.B: Or, quand Abiathar, fils d’Ahimélek, s’était enfui auprès de David à Qeïla, il était descendu avec un éphod à la main.
fr.R: Quand Abiathar, le fils d’Ahimélek, s’était échappé pour rejoindre David à Qeïla, il avait apporté un éphod avec lui. L’éphod était le vêtement du prêtre qui servait à demander des réponses à Dieu.

sw.L: Ikawa Abiathari mwana wa Ahimeleki alipokimbilia kwa Daudi [huko] Keila, efodi ilishuka mkononi mwake.
sw.B: Basi Abiathari mwana wa Ahimeleki alipokimbilia kwa Daudi huko Keila, alishuka akiwa na efodi mkononi mwake.
sw.R: Abiathari mwana wa Ahimeleki alipotoroka na kuja kwa Daudi huko Keila, alileta efodi pamoja naye. Efodi ilikuwa vazi la kuhani lililotumiwa kumwuliza Mungu majibu.

vi.L: Khi A-bi-a-tha con trai A-hi-mê-léc chạy trốn đến với Đa-vít [tại] Kê-i-la, một áo ê-phót đã xuống theo trong tay ông.
vi.B: Khi A-bi-a-tha con trai A-hi-mê-léc chạy đến với Đa-vít tại Kê-i-la, ông đã đem theo trong tay một áo ê-phót.
vi.R: Khi A-bi-a-tha con trai A-hi-mê-léc trốn thoát và đến với Đa-vít tại Kê-i-la, ông có đem theo một áo ê-phót. Áo ê-phót là áo của thầy tế lễ, dùng để cầu hỏi Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그리고 아히멜렉의 아들 아비아달이 그일라에 있는 다윗에게로 도망칠 때에, 에봇이 그의 손에 [들려] 내려왔다.
ko.B: 아히멜렉의 아들 아비아달은 그일라에 있는 다윗에게로 도망쳐 올 때에 에봇을 손에 들고 내려왔었다.
ko.R: 아히멜렉의 아들 아비아달은 도망쳐서 그일라에 있는 다윗에게 올 때에 에봇을 가지고 왔다. 에봇은 하나님께 답을 여쭐 때 쓰는 제사장의 조끼였다.

pt.L: E aconteceu que, quando Abiatar, filho de Aimeleque, fugiu para junto de Davi [em] Queila, um éfode desceu na mão dele.
pt.B: Quando Abiatar, filho de Aimeleque, fugiu para junto de Davi em Queila, ele desceu com um éfode na mão.
pt.R: Quando Abiatar, filho de Aimeleque, fugiu e foi encontrar Davi em Queila, ele levou consigo um éfode. O éfode era a veste do sacerdote usada para pedir respostas a Deus.

decisions.choice: a note looking back: how the ephod came to be with David
decisions.reason: The verse breaks off the story to explain something the reader needs for verse 9. Abiathar had escaped the killing of the priests at Nob and fled to David (22:20-23); here we learn that he joined him at Keilah and brought an ephod. The order of events is not given, so it is not clear whether David's earlier inquiries (verses 2 and 4) were made through Abiathar.

decisions.choice: ephod: the priestly garment used to seek an answer from God
decisions.reason: The ephod held the breastpiece with the Urim and Thummim, through which the LORD's will was asked (Exodus 28:6-30; see 14:3). This is probably the ephod kept at Nob, behind which Goliath's sword lay (21:10).

decisions.choice: fled to David at Keilah; an ephod came down in his hand
alternatives: he went down with David to Keilah with an ephod in his hand
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "he went down with David to Keilah, having an ephod in his hand", placing Abiathar's arrival before the battle. The Hebrew text is kept: Abiathar reached David at Keilah.

decisions.choice: came down in his hand: he carried it down with him
decisions.reason: The ephod is the grammatical subject, but the sense is that Abiathar brought it.

decisions.choice: he came down with an ephod in his hand (Balanced); he brought an ephod with him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make Abiathar the subject, since an ephod cannot come down by itself.

decisions.choice: The ephod was the priest's vest used to ask God for answers.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, as at 14:3, because verses 9-12 depend on it.

decisions.choice: el efod
decisions.reason: The priestly garment used to seek an answer from God (m2); the Samuel terms note keeps the name at every level, and Readable explains it, as the English does (r-en-2).

source.text: וַיֻּגַּ֣ד לְשָׁא֔וּל כִּי־בָ֥א דָוִ֖ד קְעִילָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֗וּל נִכַּ֨ר אֹת֤וֹ אֱלֹהִים֙ בְּיָדִ֔י כִּ֚י נִסְגַּ֣ר לָב֔וֹא בְּעִ֖יר דְּלָתַ֥יִם וּבְרִֽיחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was told to Saul that had come David [to] Keilah; and said Saul, Has made him a stranger God into my hand, for he has shut himself in by entering into a city of doors and bar.

en.L: And it was told to Saul that David had come [to] Keilah. And Saul said, "God has given him up into my hand, for he has shut himself in by entering a town of doors and bar."
en.B: Saul was told that David had gone to Keilah, and he said, "God has handed him over to me. He has shut himself in by going into a town with gates and bars."
en.R: Someone told Saul that David had gone to Keilah. Saul said, "God has handed David over to me! He has trapped himself inside a town with gates that lock."

es.L: Y se le dijo a Saúl que David había venido a Keila. Y dijo Saúl: «Dios lo ha entregado en mi mano, porque se ha encerrado al entrar en una ciudad de puertas y cerrojo».
es.B: A Saúl le avisaron que David había ido a Keila, y dijo: «Dios me lo ha entregado. Se ha encerrado al meterse en una ciudad con puertas y cerrojos».
es.R: Alguien le contó a Saúl que David había ido a Keila. Saúl dijo: «¡Dios me ha entregado a David! Él mismo se ha atrapado dentro de una ciudad con puertas que se cierran con cerrojo».

fr.L: Et on rapporta à Saül que David était venu à Qeïla. Et Saül dit : « Dieu l’a rejeté [et livré] dans ma main, car il s’est enfermé en entrant dans une ville à portes et à verrou. »
fr.B: On apprit à Saül que David était allé à Qeïla, et il dit : « Dieu me l’a livré. Il s’est lui-même enfermé en entrant dans une ville qui a des portes et des verrous. »
fr.R: Quelqu’un a dit à Saül que David était allé à Qeïla. Saül a dit : « Dieu m’a livré David ! Il s’est pris au piège dans une ville dont les portes ferment à clé. »

sw.L: Sauli akaambiwa kwamba Daudi amekuja Keila. Sauli akasema, "Mungu amemtia mkononi mwangu, kwa maana amejifungia kwa kuingia mji wenye milango na komeo."
sw.B: Sauli akaambiwa kwamba Daudi amekwenda Keila, akasema, "Mungu amemtia mikononi mwangu. Amejifungia ndani kwa kuingia katika mji wenye malango na makomeo."
sw.R: Mtu mmoja akamwambia Sauli kwamba Daudi amekwenda Keila. Sauli akasema, "Mungu amemtia Daudi mikononi mwangu! Amejinasa ndani ya mji wenye malango yanayofungwa."

vi.L: Người ta báo cho Sau-lơ rằng Đa-vít đã đến Kê-i-la. Sau-lơ nói: "Đức Chúa Trời đã bỏ nó vào tay ta, vì nó đã tự giam mình khi vào một thành có cửa và then."
vi.B: Sau-lơ được báo tin Đa-vít đã vào Kê-i-la, ông nói: "Đức Chúa Trời đã phó nó vào tay ta. Nó tự giam mình khi vào một thành có cổng và then cài."
vi.R: Có người báo cho Sau-lơ biết Đa-vít đã vào Kê-i-la. Sau-lơ nói: "Đức Chúa Trời đã giao Đa-vít vào tay ta! Nó đã tự nhốt mình trong một thành có cổng khóa chặt."

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 그일라에 왔다는 것이 사울에게 알려졌다. 그러자 사울이 말했다. "하나님께서 그를 내 손에 넘기셨다. 그가 문과 빗장이 있는 성읍에 들어가서 스스로 갇혔기 때문이다."
ko.B: 다윗이 그일라에 갔다는 소식이 사울에게 전해졌다. 사울이 말했다. "하나님께서 그를 내 손에 넘겨주셨다. 그가 성문과 빗장이 있는 성읍에 들어갔으니 스스로 갇힌 셈이다."
ko.R: 어떤 사람이 다윗이 그일라에 갔다고 사울에게 알렸다. 사울이 말했다. "하나님께서 다윗을 나에게 넘겨주셨다! 그는 성문을 잠그는 성 안에 들어가서 스스로 갇혀 버렸다."

pt.L: E contaram a Saul que Davi tinha vindo [a] Queila. E Saul disse: "Deus o abandonou na minha mão, pois ele se trancou ao entrar numa cidade de portas e tranca."
pt.B: Contaram a Saul que Davi tinha ido a Queila, e ele disse: "Deus o entregou a mim. Ele se trancou ao entrar numa cidade com portões e trancas."
pt.R: Alguém contou a Saul que Davi tinha ido a Queila. Saul disse: "Deus entregou Davi nas minhas mãos! Ele se prendeu dentro de uma cidade com portões que se trancam."

decisions.choice: has given him up: has disowned him and handed him over
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to treat someone as a stranger. With "into my hand" it means that God has cast David off and given him up to Saul.

decisions.choice: given up: the reading of the Hebrew text
alternatives: has sold him into my hand
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "has sold him", which in Hebrew differs by one letter. Both give the same sense, that God has delivered David to Saul; the Hebrew text is kept.

decisions.choice: Saul claims God's help for his hunt
decisions.reason: Saul says God is with him against David, though the reader knows the LORD has left Saul and is with David (16:14; 18:12, 14). Verse 14 answers him: "God did not give him into his hand".

decisions.choice: a town of doors and bar: a walled town whose gates are barred
decisions.reason: The double doors of a town gate were closed with a heavy beam across them. A walled town gave protection, but it also became a trap if an army surrounded it.

decisions.choice: gates and bars (Balanced); gates that lock (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced names the town's gates and the bars that held them shut. Readable says what the bars did.

decisions.choice: o abandonou na minha mão
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat someone as a stranger and so give him up (m1). "Abandonar" keeps the sense of casting David off, and "na minha mão" says to whom; Balanced and Readable say only "entregou", as the English says "handed over".

source.text: וַיְשַׁמַּ֥ע שָׁא֛וּל אֶת־כָּל־הָעָ֖ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה לָרֶ֣דֶת קְעִילָ֔ה לָצ֥וּר אֶל־דָּוִ֖ד וְאֶל־אֲנָשָֽׁיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And summoned Saul all the people for the war, to go down [to] Keilah to besiege David and his men.

en.L: And Saul summoned all the people for war, to go down [to] Keilah to besiege David and his men.
en.B: Saul called up all the troops for battle, to go down to Keilah and besiege David and his men.
en.R: So Saul called all his soldiers together for battle. He wanted to go down to Keilah and surround David and his men there.

es.L: Y convocó Saúl a todo el pueblo a la guerra, para bajar a Keila a sitiar a David y a sus hombres.
es.B: Saúl llamó a todas las tropas a la batalla, para bajar a Keila y sitiar a David y a sus hombres.
es.R: Así que Saúl reunió a todos sus soldados para la batalla. Quería bajar a Keila y rodear allí a David y a sus hombres.

fr.L: Et Saül convoqua tout le peuple pour la guerre, pour descendre à Qeïla assiéger David et ses hommes.
fr.B: Saül appela toutes ses troupes au combat, pour descendre à Qeïla et assiéger David et ses hommes.
fr.R: Alors Saül a rassemblé tous ses soldats pour la bataille. Il voulait descendre à Qeïla et encercler David et ses hommes dans la ville.

sw.L: Sauli akawaita watu wote vitani, kushuka Keila kumzingira Daudi na watu wake.
sw.B: Sauli akawaita askari wote kwa vita, ili kushuka Keila na kumzingira Daudi na watu wake.
sw.R: Basi Sauli akawakusanya askari wake wote kwa vita. Alitaka kushuka Keila na kumzunguka Daudi na watu wake huko.

vi.L: Sau-lơ triệu tập toàn dân ra trận, để đi xuống Kê-i-la vây hãm Đa-vít và những người của ông.
vi.B: Sau-lơ triệu tập toàn quân ra trận để xuống Kê-i-la vây hãm Đa-vít và thuộc hạ.
vi.R: Vậy Sau-lơ tập hợp toàn quân để ra trận. Vua muốn xuống Kê-i-la bao vây Đa-vít và thuộc hạ ở đó.

ko.L: 그리고 사울이 모든 백성을 전쟁에 불러 모아, 그일라로 내려가서 다윗과 그의 부하들을 포위하려고 했다.
ko.B: 사울은 모든 군대를 불러 모아 싸우게 했다. 그일라로 내려가서 다윗과 그의 부하들을 에워싸려는 것이었다.
ko.R: 그래서 사울은 군인들을 모두 불러 모았다. 그는 그일라로 내려가서 다윗과 그의 부하들을 그곳에 가두어 포위하려고 했다.

pt.L: E Saul convocou todo o povo para a guerra, para descer [a] Queila a fim de sitiar Davi e os seus homens.
pt.B: Saul convocou todas as tropas para a batalha, para descer a Queila e cercar Davi e os seus homens.
pt.R: Então Saul reuniu todos os seus soldados para a batalha. Ele queria descer até Queila e cercar Davi e os seus homens lá.

decisions.choice: all the people: the fighting men, the army
decisions.reason: Here "the people" are the men Saul calls out to fight, as in 11:11 and 15:4.

decisions.choice: besiege: surround the town and cut it off
decisions.reason: An army besieged a walled town by surrounding it so that no one could get in or out, until hunger forced it to give up. Saul means to trap David and his men inside.

decisions.choice: the troops (Balanced); his soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The people" means the army here; Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: וַיֵּ֣דַע דָּוִ֔ד כִּ֣י עָלָ֔יו שָׁא֖וּל מַחֲרִ֣ישׁ הָרָעָ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־אֶבְיָתָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן הַגִּ֖ישָׁה הָאֵפֽוֹד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And knew David that against him Saul [was] devising the evil, and said to Abiathar the priest, Bring near the ephod.

en.L: And David knew that Saul was devising the evil against him, and he said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod near."
en.B: When David learned that Saul was plotting harm against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod here."
en.R: David found out that Saul was planning to harm him. So he said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod here."

es.L: Y supo David que Saúl tramaba el mal contra él, y dijo al sacerdote Abiatar: «Acerca el efod».
es.B: Cuando David se enteró de que Saúl tramaba hacerle daño, le dijo al sacerdote Abiatar: «Trae aquí el efod».
es.R: David se enteró de que Saúl planeaba hacerle daño. Entonces le dijo al sacerdote Abiatar: «Trae aquí el efod».

fr.L: Et David sut que c’était contre lui que Saül tramait le mal, et il dit à Abiathar le prêtre : « Approche l’éphod. »
fr.B: Quand David apprit que Saül préparait un mauvais coup contre lui, il dit au prêtre Abiathar : « Apporte l’éphod. »
fr.R: David a appris que Saül voulait lui faire du mal. Alors il a dit au prêtre Abiathar : « Apporte l’éphod. »

sw.L: Daudi akajua kwamba Sauli alikuwa akipanga ubaya juu yake, akamwambia Abiathari kuhani, "Leta efodi karibu."
sw.B: Daudi alipojua kwamba Sauli alikuwa akipanga njama ya kumdhuru, akamwambia Abiathari kuhani, "Leta efodi hapa."
sw.R: Daudi akagundua kwamba Sauli alikuwa akipanga kumdhuru. Basi akamwambia Abiathari kuhani, "Leta efodi hapa."

vi.L: Đa-vít biết Sau-lơ đang mưu điều ác chống lại mình, nên nói với thầy tế lễ A-bi-a-tha: "Hãy đem áo ê-phót lại gần đây."
vi.B: Khi Đa-vít biết Sau-lơ đang âm mưu hại mình, ông nói với thầy tế lễ A-bi-a-tha: "Hãy đem áo ê-phót lại đây."
vi.R: Đa-vít biết được Sau-lơ đang định hại mình. Vì vậy ông nói với thầy tế lễ A-bi-a-tha: "Hãy đem áo ê-phót lại đây."

ko.L: 그리고 다윗은 사울이 자기를 해치려고 악한 일을 꾸미고 있다는 것을 알고, 제사장 아비아달에게 말했다. "에봇을 가까이 가져오십시오."
ko.B: 다윗은 사울이 자기를 해치려고 꾀하고 있다는 것을 알고, 제사장 아비아달에게 말했다. "에봇을 이리 가져오십시오."
ko.R: 다윗은 사울이 자기를 해치려는 계획을 세우고 있다는 것을 알게 되었다. 그래서 다윗은 제사장 아비아달에게 말했다. "에봇을 이리 가져오십시오."

pt.L: E Davi soube que Saul estava tramando o mal contra ele, e disse a Abiatar, o sacerdote: "Traga para perto o éfode."
pt.B: Quando Davi soube que Saul estava tramando o mal contra ele, disse ao sacerdote Abiatar: "Traga o éfode aqui."
pt.R: Davi descobriu que Saul estava planejando fazer mal a ele. Então disse ao sacerdote Abiatar: "Traga o éfode aqui."

decisions.choice: devising: planning, scheming
decisions.reason: The verb means to work out a plan, often a harmful one (Proverbs 3:29; 6:14). Saul's plan is the siege of verse 8.

decisions.choice: against him: put first for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "against him" before Saul's name: David sees that the harm is aimed at him, and the town is in danger only because of him (verse 10).

decisions.choice: bring the ephod: so that the LORD can be asked
decisions.reason: David asks for the ephod in order to put his questions to the LORD through the priest, as he does again at Ziklag (30:7-8).

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ דָּוִד֒ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שָׁמֹ֤עַ שָׁמַע֙ עַבְדְּךָ֔ כִּֽי־מְבַקֵּ֥שׁ שָׁא֖וּל לָב֣וֹא אֶל־קְעִילָ֑ה לְשַׁחֵ֥ת לָעִ֖יר בַּעֲבוּרִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said David, Yahweh, God of Israel, hearing has heard your servant that [is] seeking Saul to come to Keilah, to destroy the city on account of me.

en.L: And David said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant has surely heard that Saul is seeking to come to Keilah, to destroy the city on my account.
en.B: Then David said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant has heard for certain that Saul intends to come to Keilah and destroy the town because of me.
en.R: Then David prayed, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, I, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, have been told that Saul plans to come to Keilah. He wants to destroy the town because of me.

es.L: Y dijo David: «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de Israel, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo ha oído de cierto que Saúl procura venir a Keila, para destruir la ciudad por causa mía.
es.B: Entonces David dijo: «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de Israel, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo ha oído con certeza que Saúl piensa venir a Keila y destruir la ciudad por causa mía.
es.R: Entonces David oró: «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de Israel, a mí, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo, me han dicho que Saúl piensa venir a Keila. Quiere destruir la ciudad por causa mía.

fr.L: Et David dit : « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu d’Israël, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur a bien entendu dire que Saül cherche à venir à Qeïla pour détruire la ville à cause de moi.
fr.B: Puis David dit : « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu d’Israël, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur a appris de façon certaine que Saül a l’intention de venir à Qeïla et de détruire la ville à cause de moi.
fr.R: Ensuite, David a prié : « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu d’Israël, moi, {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur, j’ai appris que Saül veut venir à Qeïla. Il veut détruire la ville à cause de moi.

sw.L: Daudi akasema, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} amesikia hakika kwamba Sauli anatafuta kuja Keila, kuuharibu mji kwa ajili yangu.
sw.B: Kisha Daudi akasema, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} amesikia kwa hakika kwamba Sauli anakusudia kuja Keila na kuuharibu mji kwa sababu yangu.
sw.R: Kisha Daudi akaomba, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, mimi mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} nimeambiwa kwamba Sauli anapanga kuja Keila. Anataka kuuharibu mji kwa sababu yangu.

vi.L: Đa-vít thưa: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nghe rõ rằng Sau-lơ đang tìm cách đến Kê-i-la để hủy diệt thành vì cớ con.
vi.B: Rồi Đa-vít thưa: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nghe chắc chắn rằng Sau-lơ định đến Kê-i-la để hủy diệt thành vì cớ con.
vi.R: Rồi Đa-vít cầu nguyện: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, con là đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, con được báo rằng Sau-lơ định đến Kê-i-la. Ông ấy muốn hủy diệt thành này vì cớ con.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 이스라엘의 하나님, 사울이 그일라로 와서 저 때문에 이 성읍을 멸망시키려 한다는 것을 주님의 종이 분명히 들었습니다.
ko.B: 그러고 나서 다윗이 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 이스라엘의 하나님, 사울이 그일라로 와서 저 때문에 이 성읍을 멸망시키려 한다는 소식을 주님의 종이 확실히 들었습니다.
ko.R: 그러고 나서 다윗은 기도했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 이스라엘의 하나님, 주님의 종인 저는 사울이 그일라로 오려고 한다는 말을 들었습니다. 사울이 저 때문에 이 성을 없애려고 합니다.

pt.L: E Davi disse: "{{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, Deus de Israel, o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} servo certamente ouviu que Saul procura vir a Queila, para destruir a cidade por minha causa.
pt.B: Então Davi disse: "{{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, Deus de Israel, o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} servo ouviu com certeza que Saul pretende vir a Queila e destruir a cidade por minha causa.
pt.R: Então Davi orou: "{{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, Deus de Israel, eu, o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} servo, fiquei sabendo que Saul planeja vir a Queila. Ele quer destruir a cidade por minha causa.

decisions.choice: has surely heard: the doubled verb stresses that the report is certain
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats the verb to strengthen it. David is not passing on a rumor; he has heard it plainly.

decisions.choice: your servant: a humble way of saying "I"
decisions.reason: Speaking to God or to a superior, a person called himself "your servant". David uses it throughout this prayer (verse 11).

decisions.choice: to destroy the city on my account: David fears for the town
decisions.reason: Saul had already wiped out the priests' town of Nob because of David (22:19). David fears that Keilah will suffer the same.

decisions.choice: David prayed; I, your servant, have been told
decisions.reason: Readable says that David is speaking to God, and joins "your servant" to "I" so that the reader sees David means himself.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} without the article when God is addressed; {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur
decisions.reason: French drops the article in direct address, as the published French Psalms do; the possessive for God takes the deity pronoun span, as the English "your".

decisions.choice: "mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}"
decisions.reason: The possessive "wako" is a free word and takes the deity pronoun span when David speaks to God. "Your servant" stays "mtumishi" at every level, with "mimi" added at Readable as elsewhere in this block.

decisions.choice: to God, "đầy tớ của Ngài" at every level, with "con" for "me"
decisions.reason: A named servant of God says "your servant" at every level (Psalms terms note); the pronoun for God takes the deity pronoun setting, as the English "your" does.

decisions.choice: David prays in the formal polite style (합쇼체), calling himself "주님의 종" (your servant) at every level, with "저" beside it at Readable
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set: a named servant of God and the one praying say "servant" at every level; Korean has no deity_pronoun spans, and "주님" carries the respect of the English "Your".

decisions.choice: o teu servo ... ouviu
decisions.reason: David speaks to God with "tu" (as for the whole book, 1:11) and names himself in the humble third person, "o teu servo", with the verb in the third person; the span goes on "teu", which stands for God. Readable joins "eu" to the phrase, as the English does.

source.text: הֲיַסְגִּרֻ֣נִי בַעֲלֵי֩ קְעִילָ֨ה בְיָד֜וֹ הֲיֵרֵ֣ד שָׁא֗וּל כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ שָׁמַ֣ע עַבְדֶּ֔ךָ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַגֶּד־נָ֖א לְעַבְדֶּ֑ךָסוַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה יֵרֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Will surrender me [the] lords of Keilah into his hand? Will come down Saul as has heard your servant? Yahweh, God of Israel, tell, please, to your servant. And said Yahweh, He will come down.

en.L: Will the lords of Keilah surrender me into his hand? Will Saul come down as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant has heard? {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, tell {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, please." And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "He will come down."
en.B: Will the leaders of Keilah hand me over to him? Will Saul come down, as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant has heard? {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, please tell {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant." {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "He will come down."
en.R: Will the leaders of Keilah hand me over to Saul? Will Saul really come down, as I have heard? {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Israel, please tell me." {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "He will come down."

es.L: ¿Me entregarán los señores de Keila en su mano? ¿Bajará Saúl, como {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo ha oído? {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de Israel, házselo saber, te ruego, a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo». Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: «Bajará».
es.B: ¿Me entregarán los jefes de Keila en manos de él? ¿Bajará Saúl, como {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo ha oído? {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de Israel, te ruego que se lo hagas saber a {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo». {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} respondió: «Bajará».
es.R: ¿Me entregarán a Saúl los jefes de Keila? ¿De verdad bajará Saúl, como me han dicho? {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, Dios de Israel, por favor, dímelo». {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le respondió: «Sí, bajará».

fr.L: Les seigneurs de Qeïla me livreront-ils dans sa main ? Saül descendra-t-il, comme {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur l’a entendu dire ? {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu d’Israël, fais-le savoir, je te prie, à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur. » Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : « Il descendra. »
fr.B: Les notables de Qeïla me livreront-ils à lui ? Saül descendra-t-il, comme {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur l’a appris ? {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu d’Israël, fais-le savoir, je t’en prie, à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} serviteur. » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} répondit : « Il descendra. »
fr.R: Est-ce que les notables de Qeïla vont me livrer à Saül ? Est-ce que Saül va vraiment descendre, comme je l’ai entendu dire ? {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu d’Israël, dis-le-moi, s’il te plaît. » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a répondu : « Il descendra. »

sw.L: Je, wakuu wa Keila watanitia mkononi mwake? Je, Sauli atashuka kama mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} alivyosikia? Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, tafadhali mwambie mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}." {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Atashuka."
sw.B: Je, viongozi wa Keila watanitia mikononi mwake? Je, Sauli atashuka, kama mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} alivyosikia? Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, tafadhali mwambie mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}." {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akajibu, "Atashuka."
sw.R: Je, viongozi wa Keila watanitia mikononi mwa Sauli? Je, Sauli atashuka kweli, kama nilivyosikia? Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, tafadhali niambie." {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akajibu, "Atashuka."

vi.L: Các lãnh chúa của Kê-i-la có nộp con vào tay ông ấy không? Sau-lơ có xuống như đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nghe không? Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, xin cho đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết." {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Nó sẽ xuống."
vi.B: Các chức sắc của Kê-i-la có nộp con cho ông ấy không? Sau-lơ có xuống như đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã nghe không? Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, xin cho đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} biết." {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp: "Nó sẽ xuống."
vi.R: Các chức sắc của Kê-i-la có giao con cho Sau-lơ không? Sau-lơ có thật sẽ xuống đây như con đã nghe không? Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời của Y-sơ-ra-ên, xin cho con biết." {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp: "Nó sẽ xuống."

ko.L: 그일라의 지도자들이 저를 그의 손에 넘겨주겠습니까? 주님의 종이 들은 대로 사울이 내려오겠습니까? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 이스라엘의 하나님, 부디 주님의 종에게 알려 주십시오." 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다. "그가 내려올 것이다."
ko.B: 그일라의 지도자들이 저를 그에게 넘겨주겠습니까? 주님의 종이 들은 대로 사울이 내려오겠습니까? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 이스라엘의 하나님, 주님의 종에게 알려 주십시오." {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 대답하셨다. "그가 내려올 것이다."
ko.R: 그일라의 지도자들이 저를 사울에게 넘겨주겠습니까? 제가 들은 대로 사울이 정말 내려오겠습니까? {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, 이스라엘의 하나님, 저에게 알려 주십시오." {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 대답하셨다. "그가 내려올 것이다."

pt.L: Os senhores de Queila me entregarão na mão dele? Saul descerá, como o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} servo ouviu? {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, Deus de Israel, declara, por favor, ao {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} servo." E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse: "Ele descerá."
pt.B: Os líderes de Queila vão me entregar a ele? Saul vai descer, como o {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} servo ouviu? {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, Deus de Israel, por favor, revela isso ao {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} servo." {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} respondeu: "Ele descerá."
pt.R: Os líderes de Queila vão me entregar a Saul? Saul vai mesmo descer até aqui, como eu ouvi dizer? {{divine_name:SENHOR|Javé}}, Deus de Israel, por favor, responde-me." {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} respondeu: "Ele vai descer."

decisions.choice: the lords of Keilah: the town's leading citizens
decisions.reason: The word means owners or masters. Used of a town it names the landholders who governed it and could decide its policy, as "the lords of Shechem" did (Judges 9:2-3).

decisions.choice: two questions, and the LORD answers the second first
decisions.reason: David asks whether the town will give him up and whether Saul will come. The LORD answers only the second, so in verse 12 David asks the first question again.

decisions.choice: surrender: shut in and hand over
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for shutting: the town that "shut" David in (verse 7) could also hand him over. Towns under siege bought peace by giving up the man the attacker wanted (2 Samuel 20:15-22).

decisions.choice: the leaders of Keilah
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "leaders" for "lords", as at Judges 9:2, since the men are not nobles but the town's chief citizens.

decisions.choice: I; me
decisions.reason: Readable puts "your servant" in the first person, the plain sense of the polite form.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} siervo; te ruego (no span on a joined clitic)
decisions.reason: In prayer the possessive for God takes the deity pronoun setting, as the English does; “te” and the clitic in “házselo”, “dímelo” stay plain, as the Spanish notes set for clitics joined to a verb or standing in a short request. Recorded once for this block.

decisions.choice: "wakuu wa Keila" (L); "viongozi wa Keila" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The town's leading landholders (m1); "wakuu" keeps their standing at Literal, and Balanced and Readable say "leaders", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "các lãnh chúa" (L); "các chức sắc" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The town's leading citizens (m1); Literal keeps "lords", the other levels name them as town notables.

decisions.choice: "그일라의 지도자들" for "the lords of Keilah"
decisions.reason: The town's leading citizens (meaning decision m1), who would decide whether to hand David over.

decisions.choice: os senhores de Queila (L); os líderes de Queila (B, R)
decisions.reason: As Judges 9:2 in Portuguese ("os senhores de Siquém", "os líderes de Siquém"): Literal keeps the sense "owners, masters" (m1), Balanced and Readable name the town's chief citizens (also verse 12).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד הֲיַסְגִּ֜רוּ בַּעֲלֵ֧י קְעִילָ֛ה אֹתִ֥י וְאֶת־אֲנָשַׁ֖י בְּיַד־שָׁא֑וּל וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה יַסְגִּֽירוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said David, Will surrender [the] lords of Keilah me and my men into [the] hand of Saul? And said Yahweh, They will surrender.

en.L: And David said, "Will the lords of Keilah surrender me and my men into [the] hand of Saul?" And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "They will surrender [you]."
en.B: David asked again, "Will the leaders of Keilah hand me and my men over to Saul?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "They will hand you over."
en.R: David asked again, "Will the leaders of Keilah hand my men and me over to Saul?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Yes, they will."

es.L: Y dijo David: «¿Me entregarán los señores de Keila, a mí y a mis hombres, en mano de Saúl?». Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: «[Te] entregarán».
es.B: David volvió a preguntar: «¿Nos entregarán los jefes de Keila, a mí y a mis hombres, en manos de Saúl?». {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} respondió: «Te entregarán».
es.R: David volvió a preguntar: «¿Nos entregarán a Saúl los jefes de Keila, a mis hombres y a mí?». {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le respondió: «Sí, lo harán».

fr.L: Et David dit : « Les seigneurs de Qeïla me livreront-ils, moi et mes hommes, dans la main de Saül ? » Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : « Ils [vous] livreront. »
fr.B: David demanda encore : « Les notables de Qeïla me livreront-ils à Saül, moi et mes hommes ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} répondit : « Ils vous livreront. »
fr.R: David a demandé encore : « Est-ce que les notables de Qeïla vont nous livrer à Saül, mes hommes et moi ? » {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a répondu : « Oui. »

sw.L: Daudi akasema, "Je, wakuu wa Keila watanitia mimi na watu wangu mkononi mwa Sauli?" {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Watakutia."
sw.B: Daudi akauliza tena, "Je, viongozi wa Keila watanitia mimi na watu wangu mikononi mwa Sauli?" {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akajibu, "Watakutia mikononi mwake."
sw.R: Daudi akauliza tena, "Je, viongozi wa Keila watanitia mimi na watu wangu mikononi mwa Sauli?" {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akajibu, "Ndiyo, watafanya hivyo."

vi.L: Đa-vít thưa: "Các lãnh chúa của Kê-i-la có nộp con và những người của con vào tay Sau-lơ không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Họ sẽ nộp [ngươi]."
vi.B: Đa-vít lại hỏi: "Các chức sắc của Kê-i-la có nộp con và thuộc hạ của con cho Sau-lơ không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp: "Họ sẽ nộp con."
vi.R: Đa-vít lại hỏi: "Các chức sắc của Kê-i-la có giao con và người của con cho Sau-lơ không?" {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp: "Có, họ sẽ làm vậy."

ko.L: 그리고 다윗이 말했다. "그일라의 지도자들이 저와 제 부하들을 사울의 손에 넘겨주겠습니까?" 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다. "그들이 [너를] 넘겨줄 것이다."
ko.B: 다윗이 다시 여쭈었다. "그일라의 지도자들이 저와 제 부하들을 사울에게 넘겨주겠습니까?" {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 대답하셨다. "그들이 너를 넘겨줄 것이다."
ko.R: 다윗이 다시 여쭈었다. "그일라의 지도자들이 저와 제 부하들을 사울에게 넘겨주겠습니까?" {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 대답하셨다. "그렇다. 넘겨줄 것이다."

pt.L: E Davi disse: "Os senhores de Queila entregarão a mim e aos meus homens na mão de Saul?" E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse: "Eles [os] entregarão."
pt.B: Davi perguntou de novo: "Os líderes de Queila vão entregar a mim e aos meus homens nas mãos de Saul?" {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} respondeu: "Eles entregarão vocês."
pt.R: Davi perguntou de novo: "Os líderes de Queila vão entregar os meus homens e a mim a Saul?" {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} respondeu: "Sim, vão."

decisions.choice: they will surrender you: the LORD answers what would happen
decisions.reason: The answer tells what the men of Keilah would do if David stayed. David leaves (verse 13), so it does not happen. The LORD's answer lets David escape the danger rather than fixing his fate.

decisions.choice: they will surrender: the object is understood
decisions.reason: The LORD answers with the verb alone; "you" (David and his men) is understood from the question.

decisions.choice: asked again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "again", since David repeats his first question of verse 11.

decisions.choice: Yes, they will.
decisions.reason: Readable answers the yes-or-no question in the shortest natural way.

decisions.choice: Eles entregarão vocês
decisions.reason: The understood object is David and his men (m2), so the LORD, who says "tu" to David, says "vocês" here for the whole group.

source.text: וַיָּקָם֩ דָּוִ֨ד וַאֲנָשָׁ֜יו כְּשֵׁשׁ־מֵא֣וֹת אִ֗ישׁ וַיֵּצְאוּ֙ מִקְּעִלָ֔ה וַיִּֽתְהַלְּכ֖וּ בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתְהַלָּ֑כוּ וּלְשָׁא֣וּל הֻגַּ֗ד כִּֽי־נִמְלַ֤ט דָּוִד֙ מִקְּעִילָ֔ה וַיֶּחְדַּ֖ל לָצֵֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose David and his men, about six hundred man, and went out from Keilah and went about in [places] where they went about; and to Saul it was told that had escaped David from Keilah, and he ceased to go out.

en.L: And David and his men arose, about six hundred men, and went out from Keilah, and they went about wherever they went about. And it was told to Saul that David had escaped from Keilah, and he stopped going out.
en.B: So David and his men, about six hundred of them, set out and left Keilah, and they kept moving from place to place. Saul was told that David had slipped away from Keilah, and he called off the march.
en.R: So David and his men left Keilah. There were now about six hundred of them. They kept moving from one place to another. When Saul heard that David had escaped from Keilah, he did not go there after all.

es.L: Y se levantaron David y sus hombres, unos seiscientos hombres, y salieron de Keila y anduvieron por donde anduvieron. Y se le informó a Saúl que David había escapado de Keila, y dejó de salir.
es.B: Entonces David y sus hombres, unos seiscientos, se pusieron en marcha, salieron de Keila y anduvieron de un lugar a otro. Cuando le avisaron a Saúl que David se había escapado de Keila, suspendió la marcha.
es.R: Así que David y sus hombres salieron de Keila. Ya eran unos seiscientos. Andaban de un lugar a otro. Cuando Saúl supo que David se había escapado de Keila, ya no fue allá.

fr.L: Et David se leva avec ses hommes, environ six cents hommes, et ils sortirent de Qeïla et allèrent là où ils allèrent. Et on rapporta à Saül que David s’était échappé de Qeïla, et il renonça à sortir.
fr.B: David et ses hommes, environ six cents, se mirent donc en route et quittèrent Qeïla, et ils allèrent d’un lieu à l’autre. Quand on apprit à Saül que David s’était échappé de Qeïla, il renonça à son expédition.
fr.R: Alors David et ses hommes ont quitté Qeïla. Maintenant, ils étaient environ six cents. Ils allaient sans cesse d’un endroit à un autre. Quand Saül a appris que David s’était échappé de Qeïla, il n’y est finalement pas allé.

sw.L: Daudi na watu wake, kama watu mia sita, wakainuka, wakatoka Keila, wakaenda popote walipoweza kwenda. Sauli akaambiwa kwamba Daudi ameponyoka kutoka Keila, akaacha kutoka.
sw.B: Basi Daudi na watu wake, kama mia sita, wakaondoka, wakatoka Keila, wakaendelea kuhama kutoka mahali hadi mahali. Sauli alipoambiwa kwamba Daudi ameponyoka kutoka Keila, akaacha safari yake.
sw.R: Basi Daudi na watu wake wakaondoka Keila. Sasa walikuwa kama watu mia sita. Wakaendelea kuhama kutoka mahali pamoja hadi pengine. Sauli aliposikia kwamba Daudi ametoroka kutoka Keila, hakwenda huko tena.

vi.L: Đa-vít và những người của ông, khoảng sáu trăm người, đứng dậy ra khỏi Kê-i-la, và họ đi đâu thì đi. Người ta báo cho Sau-lơ rằng Đa-vít đã trốn khỏi Kê-i-la, và ông thôi không đi ra nữa.
vi.B: Vậy Đa-vít và thuộc hạ, khoảng sáu trăm người, lên đường rời khỏi Kê-i-la, và cứ đi hết nơi này đến nơi khác. Khi Sau-lơ được tin Đa-vít đã thoát khỏi Kê-i-la, ông bỏ cuộc hành quân.
vi.R: Vậy Đa-vít và thuộc hạ rời khỏi Kê-i-la. Lúc này họ có khoảng sáu trăm người. Họ cứ di chuyển hết nơi này đến nơi khác. Khi Sau-lơ nghe tin Đa-vít đã trốn khỏi Kê-i-la, ông không đến đó nữa.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗과 그의 부하들, 육백 명쯤 되는 사람이 일어나 그일라에서 나가서, 갈 수 있는 곳이면 어디든지 다녔다. 그리고 다윗이 그일라에서 피했다는 것이 사울에게 알려지자, 그는 나가기를 그만두었다.
ko.B: 그래서 다윗과 그의 부하 육백 명쯤은 일어나 그일라를 떠나서, 이곳저곳으로 옮겨 다녔다. 다윗이 그일라에서 빠져나갔다는 소식이 사울에게 전해지자, 사울은 출정을 그만두었다.
ko.R: 그래서 다윗과 그의 부하들은 그일라를 떠났다. 이제 그들은 육백 명쯤 되었다. 그들은 이곳저곳으로 계속 옮겨 다녔다. 다윗이 그일라에서 빠져나갔다는 말을 듣고, 사울은 그일라로 가지 않았다.

pt.L: E Davi e os seus homens se levantaram, cerca de seiscentos homens, e saíram de Queila, e andavam por onde andavam. E contaram a Saul que Davi tinha escapado de Queila, e ele deixou de sair.
pt.B: Então Davi e os seus homens, uns seiscentos, partiram e saíram de Queila, e ficaram andando de um lugar para outro. Contaram a Saul que Davi tinha escapado de Queila, e ele desistiu da marcha.
pt.R: Então Davi e os seus homens saíram de Queila. Agora eles já eram uns seiscentos. Eles ficaram andando de um lugar para outro. Quando Saul soube que Davi tinha escapado de Queila, desistiu de ir até lá.

decisions.choice: about six hundred men: David's band has grown
decisions.reason: About four hundred men had gathered to David at the cave of Adullam (22:2). Now there are about six hundred, the number he still has later (27:2; 30:9).

decisions.choice: went about wherever they went about: they kept on the move, with no fixed place
decisions.reason: The verb is repeated in a phrase that leaves the destination open: they went wherever they could. It pictures men on the run, not settled anywhere.

decisions.choice: he stopped going out: Saul called off the campaign
decisions.reason: "Going out" is the word for an army marching out to war. Once David was no longer shut inside Keilah, Saul's plan of verse 8 had no point.

decisions.choice: There were now about six hundred of them.
decisions.reason: Readable makes the number a sentence of its own and adds "now" to show that the band had grown since 22:2.

decisions.choice: called off the march (Balanced); did not go there after all (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what Saul's stopping meant: he gave up the march on Keilah.

source.text: וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב דָּוִ֤ד בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ בַּמְּצָד֔וֹת וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב בָּהָ֖ר בְּמִדְבַּר־זִ֑יף וַיְבַקְשֵׁ֤הוּ שָׁאוּל֙ כָּל־הַיָּמִ֔ים וְלֹֽא־נְתָנ֥וֹ אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And stayed David in the wilderness in the strongholds, and stayed in the hill country in [the] wilderness of Ziph; and sought him Saul all the days, and not gave him God into his hand.

en.L: And David stayed in the wilderness in the strongholds, and he stayed in the hill country in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul sought him all the days, but God did not give him into his hand.
en.B: David stayed in the strongholds of the wilderness, in the hill country of the wilderness of Ziph. Saul searched for him day after day, but God did not give David into his hands.
en.R: David stayed out in the wilderness, in places that were hard to reach in the hills of the wilderness of Ziph. Saul looked for him every day, but God did not let Saul catch him.

es.L: Y se quedó David en el desierto, en las fortalezas, y se quedó en la región montañosa en el desierto de Zif. Y Saúl lo buscaba todos los días, pero Dios no lo entregó en su mano.
es.B: David se quedó en las fortalezas del desierto, en la región montañosa del desierto de Zif. Saúl lo buscaba día tras día, pero Dios no lo entregó en sus manos.
es.R: David se quedó en el desierto, en lugares de difícil acceso en las colinas del desierto de Zif. Saúl lo buscaba todos los días, pero Dios no dejó que Saúl lo atrapara.

fr.L: Et David demeura dans le désert, dans les forteresses, et il demeura dans la montagne, dans le désert de Ziph. Et Saül le chercha tous les jours, mais Dieu ne le livra pas dans sa main.
fr.B: David s’installa dans les forteresses du désert, dans la région montagneuse du désert de Ziph. Saül le cherchait jour après jour, mais Dieu ne le livra pas entre ses mains.
fr.R: David est resté dans le désert, dans des endroits difficiles d’accès, dans les collines du désert de Ziph. Saül le cherchait tous les jours, mais Dieu n’a pas laissé Saül l’attraper.

sw.L: Daudi akakaa nyikani katika ngome, akakaa katika nchi ya milima katika nyika ya Zifu. Sauli akamtafuta siku zote, lakini Mungu hakumtia mkononi mwake.
sw.B: Daudi akakaa katika ngome za nyikani, katika nchi ya milima ya nyika ya Zifu. Sauli akamtafuta siku baada ya siku, lakini Mungu hakumtia Daudi mikononi mwake.
sw.R: Daudi akakaa nyikani, mahali pagumu kufikika katika milima ya nyika ya Zifu. Sauli alimtafuta kila siku, lakini Mungu hakumruhusu Sauli amkamate.

vi.L: Đa-vít ở trong hoang mạc, trong các đồn lũy, và ở trong vùng đồi núi thuộc hoang mạc Xíp. Sau-lơ tìm ông mọi ngày, nhưng Đức Chúa Trời không phó ông vào tay Sau-lơ.
vi.B: Đa-vít ở trong các đồn lũy nơi hoang mạc, trong vùng đồi núi thuộc hoang mạc Xíp. Sau-lơ lùng tìm ông ngày này qua ngày khác, nhưng Đức Chúa Trời không phó Đa-vít vào tay ông.
vi.R: Đa-vít ở ngoài hoang mạc, tại những nơi khó đến trong vùng đồi của hoang mạc Xíp. Ngày nào Sau-lơ cũng lùng tìm ông, nhưng Đức Chúa Trời không để Sau-lơ bắt được ông.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗은 광야의 요새들에 머물렀고, 십 광야의 산지에 머물렀다. 그리고 사울이 날마다 그를 찾았으나, 하나님께서 그를 그의 손에 넘겨주지 않으셨다.
ko.B: 다윗은 광야의 요새들, 곧 십 광야의 산지에 머물렀다. 사울은 날마다 그를 찾아다녔으나, 하나님께서는 다윗을 사울의 손에 넘기지 않으셨다.
ko.R: 다윗은 광야에 머물렀다. 십 광야의 산속, 사람들이 오기 어려운 곳에 있었다. 사울은 날마다 다윗을 찾아다녔지만, 하나님께서는 사울이 다윗을 잡지 못하게 하셨다.

pt.L: E Davi ficou no deserto, nas fortalezas, e ficou na região montanhosa, no deserto de Zife. E Saul o procurava todos os dias, mas Deus não o entregou na mão dele.
pt.B: Davi ficou nas fortalezas do deserto, na região montanhosa do deserto de Zife. Saul o procurava dia após dia, mas Deus não entregou Davi nas mãos dele.
pt.R: Davi ficou no deserto, em lugares difíceis de alcançar, nos montes do deserto de Zife. Saul o procurava todos os dias, mas Deus não deixou que Saul pegasse Davi.

decisions.choice: the wilderness of Ziph: dry hill country south of Hebron
decisions.reason: Ziph was a town in the hills of Judah a few miles south of Hebron (Joshua 15:55). East of it the land falls away in bare ridges and ravines toward the Dead Sea; it had pasture but few settlements, which made it a place to hide.

decisions.choice: strongholds: heights that are hard to reach
decisions.reason: The word names rugged places where people could hold out against attackers (Judges 6:2). David's camp is a natural fortress, not a built fort.

decisions.choice: God did not give him into his hand: the answer to Saul's claim
decisions.reason: In verse 7 Saul said, "God has given him up into my hand." The narrator now states the opposite, using the same picture of the hand: Saul searches without end, but God protects David.

decisions.choice: all the days: continually, day after day
decisions.reason: The phrase means the whole time, not one day only: Saul never stopped looking.

decisions.choice: places that were hard to reach; did not let Saul catch him
decisions.reason: Readable explains "strongholds" by what made them useful, as at Judges 6:2, and says plainly what "give into his hand" meant here.

decisions.choice: "십 광야" for the wilderness of Ziph
decisions.reason: The form the terms of this translation set ("십과 십 사람들").

decisions.choice: o deserto de Zife; as fortalezas (L, B)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also verses 15-24; 26:1-2): "Zife", the form of Joshua 15:55 in Portuguese, and "deserto", the Old Testament word for dry, thinly settled land, though it had pasture (m1). "Fortalezas" names natural strongholds as Judges 6:2 does (m2); Readable explains them, as the English does.

source.text: וַיַּ֣רְא דָוִ֔דכִּֽי־יָצָ֥א שָׁא֖וּל לְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אֶת־נַפְשׁ֑וֹ וְדָוִ֥ד בְּמִדְבַּר־זִ֖יף בַּחֹֽרְשָׁה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And saw David that had come out Saul to seek his life; and David [was] in [the] wilderness of Ziph at Horesh.

en.L: And David saw that Saul had come out to seek his life; and David [was] in the wilderness of Ziph at Horesh.
en.B: David saw that Saul had come out to take his life. At the time David was at Horesh in the wilderness of Ziph.
en.R: David found out that Saul had come out to kill him. At that time David was at Horesh in the wilderness of Ziph.

es.L: Y vio David que Saúl había salido a buscar su vida; y David [estaba] en el desierto de Zif, en Hores.
es.B: David vio que Saúl había salido a quitarle la vida. En ese tiempo David estaba en Hores, en el desierto de Zif.
es.R: David se enteró de que Saúl había salido para matarlo. En ese tiempo David estaba en Hores, en el desierto de Zif.

fr.L: Et David vit que Saül était sorti pour chercher sa vie ; et David [était] dans le désert de Ziph, à Horesh.
fr.B: David vit que Saül était sorti pour lui ôter la vie. David se trouvait alors à Horesh, dans le désert de Ziph.
fr.R: David a appris que Saül était sorti pour le tuer. À ce moment-là, David était à Horesh, dans le désert de Ziph.

sw.L: Daudi akaona kwamba Sauli ametoka kuitafuta nafsi yake; naye Daudi [alikuwa] katika nyika ya Zifu huko Horeshi.
sw.B: Daudi akaona kwamba Sauli ametoka ili kumwondolea uhai wake. Wakati huo Daudi alikuwa Horeshi katika nyika ya Zifu.
sw.R: Daudi akagundua kwamba Sauli ametoka ili kumwua. Wakati huo Daudi alikuwa Horeshi katika nyika ya Zifu.

vi.L: Đa-vít thấy rằng Sau-lơ đã ra đi tìm hại mạng sống mình; lúc ấy Đa-vít [ở] trong hoang mạc Xíp, tại Hô-rết.
vi.B: Đa-vít thấy Sau-lơ đã kéo ra để lấy mạng mình. Lúc ấy Đa-vít đang ở Hô-rết trong hoang mạc Xíp.
vi.R: Đa-vít biết được Sau-lơ đã kéo ra để giết mình. Lúc ấy Đa-vít đang ở Hô-rết trong hoang mạc Xíp.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗은 사울이 자기 목숨을 찾으려고 나온 것을 보았다. 그때 다윗은 십 광야 호레스에 있었다.
ko.B: 다윗은 사울이 자기 목숨을 노리고 나온 것을 알았다. 그때 다윗은 십 광야의 호레스에 있었다.
ko.R: 다윗은 사울이 자기를 죽이려고 나왔다는 것을 알게 되었다. 그때 다윗은 십 광야의 호레스에 있었다.

pt.L: E Davi viu que Saul tinha saído para buscar a vida dele; e Davi [estava] no deserto de Zife, em Horesa.
pt.B: Davi percebeu que Saul tinha saído para tirar a vida dele. Nessa ocasião Davi estava em Horesa, no deserto de Zife.
pt.R: Davi descobriu que Saul tinha saído para matá-lo. Naquele tempo Davi estava em Horesa, no deserto de Zife.

decisions.choice: David saw: the vowels of the Hebrew text
alternatives: David was afraid because Saul had come out
decisions.reason: The same consonants can be read "David was afraid" with different vowels. The Hebrew text as pointed reads "saw", meaning he learned or realized; that reading is kept. "Was afraid" would fit Jonathan's words in verse 17, "Do not be afraid".

decisions.choice: seek his life: try to kill him
decisions.reason: To "seek someone's life" is to hunt him in order to kill him (20:1; 22:23).

decisions.choice: Horesh: a place name meaning "woodland" or "thicket"
decisions.reason: The word means a wooded or scrubby place, and could be read "in the woods". Here and in verses 16, 18 and 19 it names a particular spot in the wilderness of Ziph, so it is kept as a name.

decisions.choice: found out; to kill him
decisions.reason: Readable says "found out" for "saw" in the sense of learning, and "kill him" for "seek his life".

decisions.choice: Hores
decisions.reason: The place name, perhaps meaning “thicket” (m3), in its usual Spanish form, as the English keeps it as a name.

decisions.choice: "호레스" for Horesh
decisions.reason: The usual Protestant Korean form, kept as a name; its sense ("woodland") is in the meaning decision (m3).

decisions.choice: Horesa
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also verses 16, 18, 19): the place is kept as a name, as the English keeps it (m3), in the usual Brazilian form; its meaning, "woodland", is left to the note.

source.text: וַיָּ֨קָם֙ יְהוֹנָתָ֣ן בֶּן־שָׁא֔וּל וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אֶל־דָּוִ֖ד חֹ֑רְשָׁה וַיְחַזֵּ֥ק אֶת־יָד֖וֹ בֵּאלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And arose Jonathan son of Saul and went to David [to] Horesh, and strengthened his hand in God.

en.L: And Jonathan son of Saul arose and went to David [at] Horesh, and strengthened his hand in God.
en.B: Then Saul's son Jonathan set out and went to David at Horesh, and he gave him fresh strength in God.
en.R: Then Saul's son Jonathan went to see David at Horesh. He helped David find courage by trusting in God.

es.L: Y se levantó Jonatán hijo de Saúl y fue a David [a] Hores, y fortaleció su mano en Dios.
es.B: Entonces Jonatán, el hijo de Saúl, se puso en camino y fue a ver a David en Hores, y le dio nuevas fuerzas en Dios.
es.R: Entonces Jonatán, el hijo de Saúl, fue a ver a David en Hores. Lo ayudó a recobrar el ánimo confiando en Dios.

fr.L: Et Jonathan, fils de Saül, se leva et alla vers David à Horesh, et il fortifia sa main en Dieu.
fr.B: Alors Jonathan, le fils de Saül, se mit en route et alla trouver David à Horesh, et il lui redonna des forces en Dieu.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jonathan, le fils de Saül, est allé voir David à Horesh. Il l’a aidé à reprendre courage en faisant confiance à Dieu.

sw.L: Yonathani mwana wa Sauli akainuka, akaenda kwa Daudi [huko] Horeshi, akautia nguvu mkono wake katika Mungu.
sw.B: Kisha Yonathani mwana wa Sauli akaondoka, akaenda kwa Daudi huko Horeshi, akamtia nguvu mpya katika Mungu.
sw.R: Kisha Yonathani mwana wa Sauli akaenda kumwona Daudi huko Horeshi. Akamsaidia Daudi kupata ujasiri kwa kumtumaini Mungu.

vi.L: Giô-na-than con trai Sau-lơ đứng dậy đi đến với Đa-vít [tại] Hô-rết, và làm cho tay ông mạnh mẽ trong Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Bấy giờ Giô-na-than con trai Sau-lơ lên đường đến gặp Đa-vít tại Hô-rết, và giúp ông thêm sức mạnh trong Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Bấy giờ Giô-na-than con trai Sau-lơ đến thăm Đa-vít tại Hô-rết. Ông giúp Đa-vít can đảm lên nhờ tin cậy Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 그리고 사울의 아들 요나단이 일어나 호레스에 있는 다윗에게 가서, 하나님 안에서 그의 손을 굳세게 했다.
ko.B: 그때 사울의 아들 요나단이 길을 떠나 호레스에 있는 다윗에게 가서, 하나님을 의지하도록 그에게 새 힘을 북돋아 주었다.
ko.R: 그때 사울의 아들 요나단이 호레스로 다윗을 만나러 갔다. 요나단은 다윗이 하나님을 믿고 용기를 내도록 도와주었다.

pt.L: E Jônatas, filho de Saul, se levantou e foi a Davi [em] Horesa, e fortaleceu a mão dele em Deus.
pt.B: Então Jônatas, filho de Saul, partiu e foi até Davi em Horesa, e lhe deu novas forças em Deus.
pt.R: Então Jônatas, filho de Saul, foi visitar Davi em Horesa. Ele ajudou Davi a encontrar coragem na confiança em Deus.

decisions.choice: strengthened his hand: gave him courage
decisions.reason: To strengthen someone's hands is to encourage him to act boldly (Judges 9:24; 2 Samuel 2:7; Nehemiah 2:18).

decisions.choice: in God: the strength comes from God
decisions.reason: Jonathan does not offer his own protection or his father's favor. He points David to God as the one who will keep him.

decisions.choice: son of Saul: the hunter's son comes to the hunted
decisions.reason: The narrator names Jonathan as Saul's son just when Saul is hunting David, to show how much Jonathan risks in coming.

decisions.choice: gave him fresh strength in God (Balanced); helped David find courage by trusting in God (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the idiom of the hand. Readable says how the strength was found in God: by trusting him.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו אַל־תִּירָ֗א כִּ֠י לֹ֤א תִֽמְצָאֲךָ֙ יַ֚ד שָׁא֣וּל אָבִ֔י וְאַתָּה֙ תִּמְלֹ֣ךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָנֹכִ֖י אֶֽהְיֶה־לְּךָ֣ לְמִשְׁנֶ֑ה וְגַם־שָׁא֥וּל אָבִ֖י יֹדֵ֥עַ כֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to him, Not fear, for not will find you [the] hand of Saul my father; and you will reign over Israel, and I will be to you as second; and also Saul my father knows so.

en.L: And he said to him, "Do not fear, for the hand of Saul my father will not find you. And you will reign over Israel, and I will be second to you. And even Saul my father knows this."
en.B: He said to him, "Do not be afraid. My father Saul will not lay his hand on you. You will reign over Israel, and I will be at your side as your second. Even my father Saul knows that this is so."
